home.title: Toile Blanche | Saint-Paul de Vence
home.description: 22 suites, two restaurants, and a contemporary art collection in Saint-Paul de Vence. A declared artwork by the Leroy Brothers on the Côte d'Azur.
home.heroSecond: The art is not on the walls — it is the walls.
home.heroBody: And the particular pleasure of going nowhere for a few days.
home.storyP1: The Leroy Brothers arrived in Saint-Paul de Vence in 2004 with three rooms and a long-term view.
home.storyP2: Over twenty years, they bought the neighbouring houses one by one — from neighbours who became friends. Then, when the time was right, they stopped and built the version they had always had in mind.
home.storyP3: The result is something genuinely difficult to categorise.
home.storyP4: 22 suites. Two restaurants. Three pools. 20,000m² of gardens. Saint-Paul de Vence.
home.feelingP1: Toile Blanche sits on the edge of Saint-Paul de Vence — the village that gave the world Fondation Maeght, that sheltered Picasso, Chagall and Calder — and it takes that responsibility seriously.
home.feelingP2: But not seriously in the way that makes you feel watched. The pool is warm. The rosé is cold. The art will make you stop and think, and then you will go back to the pool.
home.artDesc: The works at Toile Blanche are chosen, not accumulated. Each piece was selected by the Leroy Brothers — who are themselves artists — in conversation with the people who made them. The collection spans painting, sculpture, photography and installation. It changes. New works arrive each season.
home.artDesc2: Staying here more than once means encountering a different conversation with the same rooms.
home.tablesDesc: La Guinguette is lunch under the plane trees — rosé, grilled fish, the specific joy of eating outside in Provence. Le Restaurant is the evening version: more considered, more intimate, the kitchen at full attention. Both menus are built around what is in season, what is local, what is honest.
home.lifeDesc: Saint-Paul de Vence is three minutes on foot. Fondation Maeght is five. Beyond that — studio visits, the Art Route, the valley on a bicycle, and the particular pleasure of doing none of it.
home.newsletterTitle: A home away from home, for people who have exceptional homes. Stay in touch.
home.newsletterDesc: Not too often. Just enough. The occasional note from Saint-Paul de Vence — new arrivals in the collection, what is on the table this season, and the things worth knowing before you visit.
